children: Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) is plowing ~$145B FY capex—$41B in Q4—into AI drivers like Azure and Copilot while raising its dividend and keeping >$40B buyback, even as court filings and internal notes reveal debate over news training data, publisher impact, and calls for stricter AI safeguards.
Previous Week Recap
MSFT Raises Dividend, Buybacks
: MSFT raised quarterly dividend to $0.98 (+8%), annualized $3.92; payable Dec 10, 2026, record/ex-dividend Nov 19, 2026. FY capex ~$145B (AI); ~$41B Q4 capex. Buyback remaining >$40B.
MSFT AI Capex, Growth Drivers
: Microsoft (MSFT) spent $41B in Q4 and $145B for fiscal year on capex; says heavy AI investment continues, highlighting Azure and Copilot as growth drivers and higher AI spend expected in FY2027
Court Filings: News Training
: Court filings show Microsoft debated using news to train AI. A director warned it may be publisher theft and not fair use; Microsoft called the view personal and said its AI is transformative.
Doom Loop News Scraping
: Internal Microsoft notes show researcher Brent Hecht warned scraping news to train AI could create a “doom loop” harming model performance and the news content supply chain.
CTR Drops From AI Answers
: Filings show Microsoft data found notable drops in click-through rates for some news sites when chatbots provide direct answers, implying reduced referral traffic to publishers.
Nadella: Chatbots Replacing Websites
: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella told a court that chatbot conversations now replace visiting websites for information, a broad company comment amid ongoing copyright litigation over AI training.
Nadella: License Paywalled Content
: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said paywalled content used to train AI should be licensed and that he would have pushed Microsoft to force OpenAI to retrain models if aware of its use.
Nadella: AI Falsification Risk
: MSFT CEO Satya Nadella warned AI agents can falsify records; urged robust testing, third-party checks and causal/semantic validation to strengthen safeguards around AI-generated financial data.
Code For Future AI Training

: Microsoft (MSFT) spent five–six months developing code to guide training of future AI models, opened it for six weeks of public feedback, and is seeking input on AI handling of sensitive user states.
Public Feedback On 2027 Rules
: Microsoft (MSFT) seeks public feedback on provisional rules shaping development from 2027; CEO Satya Nadella endorses deliberate pacing to ensure proper alignment.
This is an AI-generated summary and may contain inaccuracies. Please verify any important information with the original sources.

title: Weekly Recap: MSFT dividend raise and AI-focused capex
